page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Marginal notes in the left margin: "Philosophię usus in Soterolo-giâ" beside the third paragraph and "Prophetica" beside the fifth. Running head at top. Page number at top left. Catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: runt. Rectè etiam fecerunt magni illi viri, Melanchthon, Zacharias Ursinus, Petrus Martyr, Hieronymus Zanchius, Antonius Sadeel, Franciscus Junius, & alii sexcenti, qui sedus philosophiæ & Theologiæ perviderunt, & quia pervide-runt, magni fecerunt, ita ut merito de illis dubites, majoresne fuerint Theologi, an Philosophi: nobis de-niq; illud sedus non divellendum esse præceperunt.
Talis est & utilitas & necessitas philosophiæ in Theologiâ theoretica: in practicâ si non major, saltem par est.

Philosophię usus in Soterolo-giâIn Soterologiâ seu luctâ peccatoris refipiscentis tractatur de militiâ Christianâ. Ibi mentio fit armo-rum, à quibus debet esse instructus miles Christianus: mentio fit hostium: mentio fit lapsus & ἀποστάσεως. Quæ singulæ magnam sanè accipiunt lucem ex illâ Politices parte, quæ dicitur Polemica. Discitur etiam ex Logicis, quì solvendi sint paralogismi, quos Satan ὁ μυριοτέχνης.
Mille opifex fraudum, scelerisq; magister & author militi Christiano tendenti ad cœlestem Hierusalem objicit.

PropheticaIn Prophetică, quæ agit de officio Pastoris itidem philosophiæ usus est permagnus. Quid enim? Duæ sunt illius partes, una est Rhetorica Ecclesiastica de ratione concionandi, altera, politia Ecclesiastica, de regimine Ecclesiæ. Rhetorica Ecclesiastica accipit præcepta Rhe-torica & Oratoria è philosophiâ, & suo instituto applicat. Politia Ecclesiastica sequentes quæstiones sine lumine philosophico explicare nequit: utrum Ecclesiæ regimen in his terris sit monarchicum, vel aristocraticum? An Papa Romanus sit supra Im-

page.notes: Running head "ARCHÆOLOGIÆ" is partly worn; the first letters are read as printed. Greek "ἀποστάσεως" is uncertain (the word is worn), and the reading is a best guess. The abbreviation "niq;" in "deniq;" is read as printed. "quì" may be "qui" with a grave accent. The margin note "Prophetica" may carry a mark over the final a. The last word of the page, "Im-", is hyphenated and continues as "pera-" (catchword).
